title: Lifetime pulse-cap sweep for corrupt 784-50-10 IBM-OM crossbar Adam training
hypothesis: The cumulative 64-pulse-per-cell quota is a material limiter of ten-epoch from-scratch learning, especially at Adam learning rate 3e-3 where the completed baseline blocked 1,801,247 candidate pulses. Raising the quota to 128 or removing it should improve fixed epoch-10 apparent-state accuracy and lower teacher-to-student KL at one or both matched learning rates; the higher-rate arm should benefit most if its late collapse is cap-driven.
motivation: The finalized cap-64 lr=1e-3 and lr=3e-3 baselines reached 84.4%/0.452050 and 81.2%/0.531603 apparent test accuracy/KL, respectively. Their cap diagnostics differ sharply: 6,841 versus 15,864 cells reached the lifetime quota, and 46,918 versus 1,801,247 candidate pulses were blocked. This sweep isolates the cumulative quota while reusing those artifact-verified baselines and preserving initialization, OM identities, programming stream, post-deployment published defects, data order, ten epochs, and apparent-forward/persistent-update semantics.

arms.description: Adam lr=1e-3 with a 128-pulse cumulative quota per cell.
Adam lr=1e-3 with no cumulative per-cell pulse quota.
Adam lr=3e-3 with a 128-pulse cumulative quota per cell.
Adam lr=3e-3 with no cumulative per-cell pulse quota.

completion_criteria: All four declared configs complete exactly once through the native ebl runner on CUDA and pass artifact verification.
At each learning rate, the new resolved scientific configs differ from the corresponding finalized cap-64 source config only in recovery.pulse_cap_per_cell, set to 128 or null.
Every run consumes ten ordered epochs of 55,000 ground-truth-labelled examples: 3,438 minibatches per epoch, 34,380 optimizer steps, and no checkpoint selection.
Every gradient and metric-producing device forward uses held apparent q, every pulse updates hidden persistent q, and touched apparent states are refreshed after writes.

Headline metrics are fixed epoch-10 apparent-state accuracy and teacher-to-crossbar KL on the same first 1,000 official MNIST test examples as the finalized cap-64 baselines. Persistent-state accuracy/KL are secondary diagnostics.

Each epoch records cumulative optimizer pulses, maximum pulses per cell, cells at cap, and blocked pulses. Null means no lifetime quota and must produce zero cells-at-cap and zero blocked-at-cap by construction.
This remains a one-assignment, one-programming-stream exploratory fitted-preset result; it is not promoted to paper evidence, an array-level uncertainty estimate, or a fabricated-device claim.
analysis_plan: Verify CUDA execution and exact matching of logical-weight hash, sampled-population fingerprint, healthy P0 hashes, published fault mask, faulted pretraining hashes, data cohorts, optimizer steps, and all non-cap resolved settings against each corresponding finalized cap-64 baseline.

At each learning rate compare caps 64, 128, and none using fixed epoch-10 apparent accuracy as the primary endpoint and apparent teacher KL as the preferred distributional endpoint; report teacher agreement and cross-entropy beside them.
Report persistent-state accuracy/KL separately, never as the headline, on the identical test examples.

Report total/per-layer pulses, commanded cells, maximum pulses per cell, probability clipping, cells at cap, and blocked pulses. Use per-epoch cumulative telemetry to identify when cap-128 first binds; null is the exact no-lifetime-quota control.

Call the 64-pulse quota materially limiting only if a higher-cap matched arm improves apparent accuracy by at least 1 percentage point or lowers apparent KL by at least 0.05 without losing more than 1 percentage point of accuracy. Otherwise report the numerical sensitivity without claiming a material cap effect.
Treat any benefit at lr=3e-3 that does not close the gap to lr=1e-3 as evidence that learning-rate dynamics, not only the cap, limit the higher-rate run.
